title: Noor and the Oath
premise: Tamsin Ashgrove, a mercenary bound by oath to a god who has gone silent, keeps the ledgers of the Gilded Ledger, a guild that trades in impossible things. When a dying stranger presses a map into their hands, Tamsin discovers it charts the resting place of the Oathstone — the relic that once anchored every sworn god's voice, and whose theft caused the silence. Hunted by the Hollow Order, who want to shatter the stone forever, Tamsin gathers a found family of debtors and deserters and races to reach it first. In the end, Tasmash must choose: restore the god that abandoned them, or break their own oath and give the stone's power to the people who earned it.
about_author: Tamsin Hartwell is a former archivist who left academia to write fantasy about broken promises and stubborn survivors. They live on a windswept coast with two cats and an ever-growing collection of unread maps.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unpaid Debts
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. While auditing the guild's strangest accounts, Tamsin is ambushed by a dying courier who presses a bloodstained map into their hands and whispers 'the stone still sings.' The Hollow Order arrives minutes later, burning the shop. Emotional beat: reluctant responsibility — Tamsin wants no part of gods or wars, but survival has just become inheritance.

chapters.title: A Company of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, with interludes from Sefa, a disgraced guild debtor. Fleeing along the map's route, Tamsin assembles an unlikely crew: Sefa, a deserter knight, and a cartographer who lies beautifully. The Order's hunters close in, and Tamsin's silent god flickers for the first time in years. Emotional beat: guarded trust hardening into something like family.

chapters.title: Where the Stone Still Sings
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the Oathstone's hidden vault beneath a drowned cathedral, the crew learns the truth: the gods didn't abandon their oaths — the Order stole their voices to free humanity, at terrible cost. The Order offers Tamsin a place among them; their god offers forgiveness. Climax: betrayal within the crew forces Tamsin to choose allegiance mid-battle as the vault collapses.

chapters.title: What We Swear to Each Other
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Wounded but victorious, Tamsin refuses both the Order's nihilism and the god's bargain, instead splitting the Oathstone's power among mortals — making every vow a human act again. The old god fades, whispering thanks. The found family rebuilds the guild around honest debts. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — survival was never free, but it can be shared.
